Messages.Author: Brian D. Leist
Messages.Body:
Rotschrek (sp?) is played when a minion (ally or vampire) is about
to do aggravated damage to a vampire. The vampire (the one taking) the aggraaggravated damage is placed in torpor and combat ends. This is meant
to be used to save a vampire from being burned by aggravated damage.
and just sends the vampire to torpor with no damage being dealt. It is
after all an out-of-turn card to be used when other people are acting
against you.
-Brian

I don't see how it would matter that it's an out-of-turn master card
-- you can still play it on either combatant. If you have the flamethrower,
you'll be the one doing aggravated damage. Remember the "whether
successfully or not" phrase -- you can use it when the other vampire
dodges.

Also, as often happens with Frenzy, a third Methuselah may well wish to
play this card on either combatant, cackling madly all the while.

(And yes, I know there's a "ruling" that Ro"tschreck does the opposite
of what it says. For something that contradicts the wording of a card,
I expect a WotC erratum.)

Messages.Author: Stephen Young
Messages.Body:
Rotschreck is, by definition, an intense fear of "sunlight." I would
agree that the spirit of the card is to put into torpor the vampire about
to recieve aggrivated damage (OH, NO! you're going to put a stake through
my heart? I'm so scared I'll just drop right into torpor before you can
do it! :( aak!)

The wording (minion vs. vampire) seems to support this.

Steve

Messages.Author: Thomas R Wylie
Messages.Body:
Actually, Rotschreck is a general fear of overly lethal things. The classic
example is sunlight, but fire and such are included as well.

The concept behind the Rotschreck card in Jyhad is that a Methuselah sees
a vampire playing with such naughty toys, and confronts the vampire with the
horror of just what it's doing. That vampire then goes and hides for
a while.

Messages.Author: Owen Reynolds
Messages.Body:
>Actually, Rotschreck is a general fear of overly lethal things. The classic
>example is sunlight, but fire and such are included as well.

>The concept behind the Rotschreck card in Jyhad is that a Methuselah sees
>a vampire playing with such naughty toys, and confronts the vampire with the
>horror of just what it's doing. That vampire then goes and hides for
>a while.

That's an amazingly horrible explaination for several reasons. Most
obvious is that the card is clearly written to work the other way. Secondly
is, what's wrong with aggravated damage? If they didn't like it, they
could have agreed not to allow it in their little game (the Jyhad they are
having.)
Lastly, the reason that is most silly -- the Methusalahs remain hidden
and secret for a reason. They are terrified of being found, caught and
slain by other powerful vampires. As a vampire card, they'd be archons
with 4+ disciplines at double superior and a 25 capacity, etc, etc... but
they do not become personally involved.
I can't imagine them voilating their centuries-long carefully kept
anonymity to walk up to a guy with claws and say, "hey -- that could put
an eye out."

Aggravated damage is great. What's wrong with having a card to hose

cards to hose those.

Methusaleh is the one jumping out of the alley and confronting the vampire;
perhaps they are having some minion doing it.
